$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs the same steps locally.
Same shape as picard-rs and htsjdk-rs; see picard-rs decision 0008 for why a golden that no
CI step re-derives is not evidence.

ci.$why: Suites share a job because each job restores the oracle image once.

suites.title: ReadFilterLibrary decisions
suites.why: One row per filter, one character per record: the reference's own decision, taken through SAMRecordToGATKReadAdapter rather than off the flags. Going through the adapter is the point: GATKRead.isUnmapped is three criteria and isFirstOfPair requires pairing, so comparing against flags would compare against a reimplementation of the adapter instead of the reference. The corpus travels in the same file as SAM text, so the port judges the records the reference judged rather than a description of them.
suites.$compare_why: Line mode, not keyed. Keyed compares one row per (kind, case) pair, and every dump here repeats a kind across many cases: the ReadClipper golden has 2,385 rows and only 181 distinct keys, so keyed mode silently compared 8% of it and reported ok. The whole file is the artefact and its order is part of it.

cases.why: ReadUtils maps a reference position to a read offset, and every walker, annotation and clipping operation stands on that arithmetic. It is probed from three bases before each read to three past it, so the not-found answers at both edges are measured rather than assumed.

Every cigar ReadClipper produces goes through CigarUtils.clipCigar and CigarBuilder, and the builder rewrites what it is handed: it merges, drops zero-length elements, removes deletions that land at either end, and moves a deletion that arrives after an insertion in front of it. Each rewrite is a byte difference in the output BAM of every clipping tool.

Clipping rewrites the read: bases, qualities, cigar, alignment start and, for a flow read group, some of its tags. The golden carries the whole clipped read for every entry point, because comparing one field would hide the others.

The bases a tool sees are not the bytes in the FASTA: CachingIndexedFastaSequenceFile upper-cases every query and flattens every IUPAC code to N. The fixture travels in the golden so the port reads the bytes the reference read, and the comparison covers the transformation rather than the file format.

CountingReadFilter's summary text is output a tool prints, so it is compared as bytes. It is also the only place the order of a conjunction is observable: the boolean cannot say which of WellformedReadFilter's eight filters rejected a read, and the counts can.

suites.title: ReadsDataSource interval queries
suites.why: Which reads a walker sees for a given -L is decided by htsjdk's stateful query filter, not by an overlap test: its interval index only advances and the traversal stops once every interval is behind the record, unmapped reads carrying their mate's position are special-cased, and QueryInterval.optimizeIntervals merges abutting intervals so two adjacent -L arguments return a spanning read once. The fixture BAM and its .bai travel in the golden as base64, so the port queries the bytes the reference queried.

cases.why: Produced by the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner and downloaded from that run's artifact, which is the only provenance this programme accepts for a golden. Three of its answers are worth naming: a query at 500-500 does not return the mapped read that starts at 500 with an empty cigar, because its alignment end is 499; a query at 495-505 does; and 499-499 stops the traversal outright.

suites.title: ReferenceContext windows
suites.why: A walker never queries the reference directly: it is handed a window around its position, and three of that window's behaviours are decisions. Near a contig edge the window is silently smaller than requested and numWindowLeadingBases reports what was obtained rather than what was asked for; getBases(leading, trailing) expands the window rather than the interval, so the expansions compose; and getKmerAround returns null rather than a shorter kmer when the edge prevents expansion. Each accessor gets its own row, so which call throws is measured rather than collapsed into one E.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. Its sharpest row is the asymmetry between the two ways of asking for the same window: setWindow(3, 3) at chr1:1-1 crops silently to chr1:1-4, while the same window given as coordinates throws, because building SimpleInterval(chr1, -2, 4) is itself the error.
